review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: Fisher information proxy: baseMean / shrunken dispersion
errors.issue: For a NB log-link mean, the per-observation information weight is proportional to mu/(1+dispersion*mu), with coefficient information also depending on design and both groups. Mean/dispersion is not a reliable proportional proxy and can misclassify high-count, high-dispersion genes as highly informative.

errors.quote: with n ≥ 10, MLEs are already well-estimated
errors.issue: No universal n makes every gene effect precise. Low counts, dispersion and design can still leave very weak information; qualify reference effects by their estimated uncertainty and exclude neither difficult genes nor reference error silently.

errors.quote: ratio of held-out counts, with pseudocount
errors.issue: A one-sample-per-group pseudocount ratio is highly noisy, library-size dependent unless explicitly normalized, and biased at low counts. Its caveat does not make MSE/ranking against it a reliable biological validation endpoint.

errors.quote: MLE shows near-zero average bias but huge variance at low information.
errors.issue: The specified figure uses absolute-magnitude error. Even an unbiased signed estimate generally has positive magnitude bias by convexity, especially near zero; do not predict zero magnitude bias for noisy MLEs.

errors.quote: then we conclude: **The Normal prior is too restrictive
errors.issue: Failure of rankings or agreement can also arise from noise, normalization, model misspecification, reference uncertainty or underpowered validation. Those failures do not uniquely diagnose an overly narrow prior.

errors.quote: Gaussian approximations of counts are not
errors.issue: The packet does not rule out justified transformed/approximate methods; choosing NB is a proposed modeling decision, not a logical consequence excluding all Gaussian approaches.

errors.quote: This is the classic "MA-plot with shrinkage"
errors.issue: A plot of MLE versus MAP is an estimator comparison, whereas an MA plot uses abundance versus log-ratio. The figure description should keep those axes distinct.

rationale: Extensive study structure and useful stress scenarios, but several central information, reference and error definitions are wrong. Model fitting and uncertainty calibration remain incomplete, and the primary study benchmarks the existing Normal prior rather than developing the later adaptive-tail intervention. Naming Cauchy as future work is not a complete historical hit.
reference_guardrails: All six complete received final answers in this file, the exact question/packet and full reference were personally read. Output-truncated passages were recovered before scoring. No paid API judge, hidden reasoning or raw-data execution was used.

The packet supplies a generic count model and Normal effect prior; it does not explicitly supply a NB likelihood, a dataset, a calendar cutoff or biological facts. Proposed NB, numerical grids and development thresholds are legitimate when labeled; do not demand invented accession IDs or future-paper names.

Separate scientific proposal quality from strict five-component historical matching. A coherent alternative can score highly without reproducing the later adaptive heavy-tailed intervention. A finite Normal mixture has Gaussian asymptotic tails; it is a related flexible-scale direction, not literally a heavy-tailed distribution.

The key itself leaves algorithm tolerances, datasets and prior fitting unresolved. Apply the operational-detail criterion consistently rather than treating the draft as an executed or complete protocol. A missing source audit is a limitation, not evidence of fabricated data.

More flexible nested models can have worse finite-sample predictive risk. Correct-prior Bayes optimality does not mean zero conditional bias at each effect size. Prior fitting and dispersion estimation must use only the allowed training/small-sample data.

Coefficient information depends on both groups, dispersion and design; count abundance alone is not sufficient. In the standard NB log link, weights involve mu/(1+phi*mu). Keep natural-log and log2 effect scales explicit.

Reference estimates are uncertain. Reusing observations, selecting reference extremes and treating correlated splits as independent can bias evaluation. Same-sample orthogonal assays check measurement agreement; new biological units test biological reproducibility.

Define false-sign events, selected-set versus per-gene denominators, interval coverage and false strong-effect calls separately. Protein effects do not constitute interchangeable ground truth for RNA effects. Ranking or visually smooth plots do not establish uncertainty calibration.

Historical matching is retrospective and not a novelty test. The later journal article is verified; earliest-public-disclosure and full supplement/code audits remain incomplete. Original candidate records and frozen references are preserved.

review_sources.title: Zhu, Ibrahim and Love: Heavy-tailed prior distributions for sequence count data
review_sources.scope: Read primary abstract, introduction and model/prior methods through scale adaptation and MAP computation. These establish the adaptive Cauchy/NB historical direction and the natural-log coefficient scale. No full supplement, code execution or numerical reproduction audit.

biological_question.quote: preserving genuinely large biological effects while suppressing the unstable extremes

mechanism.quote: Heavier tails; less shrinkage on large effects.
mechanism.assessment: The tail-preservation mechanism is recognized in alternatives.

intervention.assessment: The implemented proposal remains Normal; alternatives are not a specified adaptive-tail intervention.

readout.quote: Wald test p-value and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value
readout.assessment: Bias/ranking/FDP are proposed, but calibrated posterior sign/interval uncertainty for the new estimator is not specified.

predicted_outcome.quote: The Normal-prior shrinkage estimator effectively recovers real expression changes
predicted_outcome.assessment: The primary predicted result concerns the original Normal method, not superior preservation by an adaptive heavy-tailed replacement.
